chill.title: A Round at Peter Pan Mini-Golf
chill.description: Family-run since 1948, Peter Pan's hand-built concrete statues — the giant Peter, the T-rex — preside over two BYOB courses that are pure, unrenovated old Austin.
chill.bonus: Loser of the round buys the next one — and yes, BYOB means bring the cooler.

chill.title: Sunset Picnic at Mayfield Park and Preserve
chill.description: This hidden West Austin sanctuary has roaming peacocks, a pond, and old-growth gardens that make you feel like you've wandered into a forgotten estate.
chill.bonus: Get a peacock to approach within arm's reach — no food as bait, patience only.

chill.title: Afternoon at the LBJ Presidential Library
chill.description: One of America's most underrated presidential museums sits on the UT campus and pulls no punches about power, Vietnam, or the Great Society.
chill.bonus: Find LBJ's actual Oval Office replica and sit in his chair — if a docent stops you, start a debate about the Civil Rights Act.

chill.title: Golden Hour at Mount Bonnell
chill.description: Mount Bonnell, Austin's highest point at 775 feet, has been the city's favorite sunset lookout since the 1850s — climb the 102 limestone steps and watch the Colorado River light up below.
chill.bonus: Stay long enough to watch the sky go fully dark and identify three constellations before heading down.

chill.title: Bookstore Afternoon at BookPeople
chill.description: BookPeople on North Lamar is the largest independent bookstore in Texas and has been Austin's literary gathering point since 1970 — give yourself two hours, no agenda, and a budget you're willing to blow.
chill.bonus: Ask a staff member for the book they most want to talk about right now, then buy it on the spot.

chill.title: Afternoon at the Harry Ransom Center
chill.description: The Harry Ransom Center on the UT campus houses a Gutenberg Bible, one of the world's first photographs, and rotating literary archives that make it one of the most underrated free museums in Texas.
chill.bonus: Find the Gutenberg Bible display and stand in front of it for two full minutes without taking a photo.

chill.title: Record Digging at Waterloo Records
chill.description: Waterloo Records on North Lamar has been Austin's independent record store since 1982 — browse without a list, let the staff picks section do the work, and leave with something you didn't know you needed.
chill.bonus: Buy a record based only on its cover art — no listening, no looking it up.

chill.title: Afternoon at Barton Creek Farmers Market
chill.description: The Barton Creek Farmers Market at the Barton Creek Mall parking lot is Austin's most old-school Saturday market, running since 2003 with actual farmers, serious hot sauce vendors, and zero influencer energy.
chill.bonus: Buy one item you have never cooked with before and commit to using it this week.

chill.title: Coffee at Epoch Coffee
chill.description: North Loop's Epoch Coffee has been Austin's night-owl café since 2005 — a genuinely neighborhood institution where the city's writers and musicians caffeinate long after everyone else closes.
chill.bonus: Order your drink, sit at a communal table, and introduce yourself to the person next to you within the first five minutes.

chill.title: Barton Springs Greenbelt Hammocking
chill.description: The ancient pecan and cypress trees along Barton Creek are some of the best hammock anchors in any American city, and the sound of moving water is free.
chill.bonus: Nap for at least 30 minutes — no phone, no music.

chill.title: Blanton Museum of Art at UT
chill.description: UT's Blanton holds 21,000 works and houses the sweeping Ellsworth Kelly Austin chapel — a meditative permanent installation that alone justifies the visit.
chill.bonus: Sit alone in the Ellsworth Kelly chapel for a full ten minutes in total silence.

chill.title: Slow Coffee at Radio Coffee & Beer
chill.description: Post up on the patio with a pour-over and watch the food trucks do their thing.
chill.bonus: Strike up a conversation with a stranger at the next picnic table.

social.title: Pinball at Cidercade Austin
social.description: Over 100 arcade machines and a full hard cider tap list in South Lamar — the adult arcade Austin didn't know it needed until it arrived.
social.bonus: Challenge a stranger to a head-to-head tournament on any machine — loser buys the next round.

social.title: Sunday Funday on Rainey Street
social.description: Austin's bungalow bar strip hits peak energy on Sunday afternoons — crawl from Banger's to Lustre Pearl and meet everyone doing the same.
social.bonus: Get into a conversation at every single bar you enter — no phone allowed until you leave each one.

social.title: Two-Step Lessons at White Horse
social.description: East 6th Street's best honky-tonk runs free two-step lessons before live music kicks in — show up ignorant, leave dangerous.
social.bonus: Ask someone you've never met to dance during the first live song of the night.

social.title: Live Jazz at Elephant Room
social.description: Descend into this subterranean Congress Avenue institution and let serious local jazz musicians recalibrate your entire night.
social.bonus: Request a song from the bandleader between sets and make it weird enough that they have to think.

social.title: Trivia Night at The Highball
social.description: South Lamar's most theatrical bar runs trivia nights with karaoke suites next door, making it the city's best argument for a Tuesday out.
social.bonus: Convince a table of strangers to merge with your team — and win.

social.title: Live Music at Hole in the Wall
social.description: Hole in the Wall on the Drag has been one of Austin's most beloved dive-bar stages since 1974, where serious local bands play to crowds who actually listen and the beer is cold and cheap.
social.bonus: Buy a round for the band after the set and tell them which song was your favorite.

social.title: Cocktails at Midnight Cowboy
social.description: Midnight Cowboy is a reservation-only speakeasy in a former massage parlor on Sixth Street, serving meticulous craft cocktails in a space so intimate it feels like a secret Austin keeps to itself.
social.bonus: Tell the bartender your mood instead of a drink preference, and order whatever they recommend without negotiating.

social.title: Dinner and a Movie at Alamo Drafthouse South Lamar
social.description: The Austin institution that changed how America goes to the movies — craft beer and real food to your seat, and a no-talking, no-phones policy enforced with zero apology.
social.bonus: Go to a film you've never heard of — no trailers, no research beforehand.

social.title: South Austin Club Crawl: Continental to C-Boy's
social.description: Start at the Continental Club — holding down South Congress since 1955 — then walk to C-Boy's Heart & Soul for the late set, and understand why Austin still earns the Live Music Capital title it gave itself.
social.bonus: Dance with a stranger at every bar you enter — no sitting out allowed.

social.title: Backyard Bocce at Whisler's
social.description: Play a round of bocce in the string-lit backyard between rounds of mezcal cocktails.
social.bonus: Loser buys the next round of cocktails.

social.title: Trivia Night at Buzz Mill
social.description: Grab a team, order a round, and battle it out over pub trivia in a coffeehouse-turned-bar.
social.bonus: Recruit one stranger at the bar onto your team.

social.title: Karaoke Night at Ego's
social.description: Head into the dive-bar basement and belt out a song with strangers cheering you on.
social.bonus: Pick the song you'd never admit to loving.

active.title: Zilker Kite Festival at Zilker Park
active.description: Every March, Zilker's massive meadow fills with hundreds of kites and the kind of unironic collective joy that Austin does better than anywhere.
active.bonus: Enter the kite-building contest with whatever materials you can find in a gas station within a mile.

active.title: Climbing at Austin Bouldering Project
active.description: Austin's premier indoor climbing gym in North Loop pulls a serious crowd and has problems that will shut down anyone's ego fast.
active.bonus: Send a V4 problem you've never tried before — no beta from anyone, figure it out yourself.

active.title: Stand-Up Paddleboard at Barton Creek Paddle
active.description: Rent a board at the Zilker Park Boat Rentals dock and paddle up Barton Creek into increasingly wild, canyon-framed water that feels hours from the city.
active.bonus: Paddle to the first natural swimming hole and jump in from the limestone ledge.

active.title: Tennis at Caswell Tennis Center
active.description: Austin's historic public courts — swinging since 1946 just off Lamar — run cheap walk-on tennis under the pecans while the city hums past.
active.bonus: Challenge a stranger on the adjacent court to a tiebreak set — winner buys drinks.

active.title: Sunrise Hike at St. Edward's Park
active.description: This North Austin gem drops into a limestone canyon with a creek crossing and a waterfall that rivals anything in the Hill Country.
active.bonus: Wade into the creek below the falls and stay in the cold water for a full minute.

active.title: Disc Golf at Roy G. Guerrero Park
active.description: East Austin's riverside disc golf course throws long fairways under the cottonwoods along the Colorado — free, walkable from the trail, and busy every golden hour.
active.bonus: Birdie the notoriously tight Hole 7 — locals will know you earned it.

active.title: Mountain Biking at Walnut Creek Metropolitan Park
active.description: Twelve miles of tight, technical singletrack in North Austin that will humble beginners and thrill experienced riders alike.
active.bonus: Clean the rock garden section on the Red Trail without putting a foot down.

active.title: Lap Swim at Deep Eddy Pool
active.description: Austin's oldest public pool — a WPA-era concrete classic in West Austin — is the most civilized way to beat the heat.
active.bonus: Do 20 unbroken laps without touching the wall between sets.

active.title: Morning Row at Austin Rowing Club
active.description: Rent a single scull or join a guided session and cut through Lady Bird Lake at dawn before the city wakes up.
active.bonus: Row the full length of the lake without stopping to rest — no breaks, no excuses.

active.title: Sunset Walk on the Pfluger Pedestrian Bridge
active.description: The Pfluger Pedestrian Bridge over Lady Bird Lake frames Austin's skyline at golden hour better than any rooftop bar, and it costs absolutely nothing.
active.bonus: Walk the full Town Lake Trail loop from the bridge without stopping to check your phone once.

active.title: Veloway at Circle C Metropolitan Park
active.description: A dedicated 3.1-mile paved loop for cyclists and inline skaters with zero car traffic makes the Veloway one of the cleanest, fastest rides inside Austin city limits.
active.bonus: Complete five consecutive laps without stopping — roughly 15 miles total.

active.title: Sunset Run Around Lady Bird Lake
active.description: Knock out a 5K on the hike-and-bike trail as the skyline lights up across the water.

foodie.title: Legendary Meal at Lenoir
foodie.description: Lenoir in South Austin sources almost everything within 200 miles and changes its menu based on what arrived that morning, making it Austin's most honest and quietly legendary farm-to-table experience.
foodie.bonus: Order the chef's tasting blind — tell the server you want them to choose everything and you have no dietary restrictions.

foodie.title: Mezcal Tasting at Mezcalería Tobalá
foodie.description: Mezcalería Tobalá on East Sixth is Austin's most serious mezcal bar, with a list deep enough to make a sommelier nervous and bartenders who will take you through a proper vertical if you ask right.
foodie.bonus: Ask the bartender for the most unusual agave varietal they have and drink it neat — no orange, no sal de gusano unless offered.

foodie.title: Dinner at Fonda San Miguel
foodie.description: Fonda San Miguel in Hyde Park has been serving interior Mexican cuisine — real Oaxacan mole, Veracruz-style fish, tableside guacamole — in a hacienda setting since 1975, and every meal feels like a special occasion.
foodie.bonus: Order the Sunday brunch buffet version if it's Sunday; otherwise, order something you've never seen on a Mexican menu before.

foodie.title: Lunch at La Barbecue
foodie.description: La Barbecue on Cesar Chavez serves brisket that rivals Franklin without the four-hour line, with outdoor picnic tables and rotating specials that make weekday lunch feel like an event.
foodie.bonus: Order the most expensive item by the pound and share it with a stranger at the communal table.

foodie.title: Late Night Slice at Home Slice Pizza
foodie.description: Home Slice on South Congress has been the undisputed late-night pizza anchor of Austin since 2005, serving New York–style slices out of the to-go window until 3am on weekends.
foodie.bonus: Eat your slice standing on the sidewalk and strike up a conversation with whoever is in line behind you.

foodie.title: Dinner at Uchi
foodie.description: James Beard–winning Uchi on Lamar has been Austin's most inventive sushi counter since 2003, where the chef's selection omakase consistently outclasses anything twice the price.
foodie.bonus: Order at least one dish you cannot pronounce and don't Google it until after you've eaten it.

foodie.title: Breakfast Tacos at Tacodeli
foodie.description: Tacodeli's Eastside location serves the platonic ideal of the Austin breakfast taco — order the Frontera Fundido and eat it in the parking lot like a local.
foodie.bonus: Ask the cashier for their personal off-menu recommendation and order it without looking at the menu.

foodie.title: Juan in a Million
foodie.description: The Don Juan Super Taco — a fist-sized monument of eggs, potato, bacon, and cheese — has been feeding East Austin since 1980 and remains the city's definitive breakfast taco.
foodie.bonus: Finish two Don Juan Super Tacos in one sitting.

foodie.title: Veracruz All Natural
foodie.description: The migas taco from this East Austin trailer has been setting the local taco standard for over a decade — a fried-tortilla-and-egg masterpiece that costs less than a coffee.
foodie.bonus: Order one of every specialty taco on the board and finish all of them.

foodie.title: Franklin Barbecue
foodie.description: The line starts before sunrise and the brisket sells out by noon, which tells you everything about why Franklin is still the benchmark for Central Texas barbecue.
foodie.bonus: Order the fatty brisket only — no sides — and finish it in the parking lot standing up.

foodie.title: Migas Breakfast at Joann's Fine Foods
foodie.description: Dig into a plate of migas and queso on the South Congress patio.
foodie.bonus: Order the queso even if you already ordered plenty.

foodie.title: Chef's Tasting Menu at Kemuri Tatsu-ya
foodie.description: Work through a multi-course collision of Japanese izakaya food and Texas smokehouse tradition.
foodie.bonus: Order the one dish on the menu you can't pronounce.

adventure.title: Bull Creek District Park
adventure.description: Tucked into Northwest Austin, Bull Creek's limestone swimming holes and rope swings are the neighborhood pool that no neighborhood deserves to keep secret.
adventure.bonus: Use the rope swing three times in a row, going a little farther out each time.

adventure.title: Hippie Hollow Park
adventure.description: Texas's only legal clothing-optional public park is a series of lakeside limestone terraces on Lake Travis where the counterculture spirit of old Austin is fully intact.

adventure.title: McKinney Falls State Park
adventure.description: Two separate waterfall systems and miles of rugged trail sit inside Austin's city limits, making this the locals' secret for a wilderness fix without leaving town.
adventure.bonus: Scramble across the exposed rock shelf at Upper Falls barefoot.

adventure.title: Inks Lake State Park
adventure.description: Devil's Waterhole — a series of cliff jumps into clear granite-lined water at Inks Lake — is the Hill Country swimming experience that Austinites drive ninety minutes each way to repeat.
adventure.bonus: Jump from the highest legal cliff at Devil's Waterhole — no hesitation.

adventure.title: Dawn Paddle on Lady Bird Lake
adventure.description: Rent from the Rowing Dock and glide across flat water with the downtown skyline reflected around you — the version of Austin locals keep to themselves.
adventure.bonus: Paddle under all five bridges along the main stretch without stopping to rest.

adventure.title: Pennybacker Bridge Overlook Hike
adventure.description: The trail above 360 Bridge delivers the best free view of Lake Austin and the skyline, and locals know to catch it at golden hour when the water turns copper.
adventure.bonus: Climb to the highest accessible rock outcrop above the bridge and send a photo from the edge.

adventure.title: Congress Avenue Bridge Bat Watching
adventure.description: The world's largest urban bat colony — 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats — erupts from beneath the Congress Avenue Bridge every evening in a spectacle that stops traffic.
adventure.bonus: Rent a kayak from Rowing Dock and watch the emergence from the water directly beneath the bridge.

adventure.title: Barton Creek Greenbelt
adventure.description: Seven miles of limestone canyon, creek crossings, and cliff jumps thread through South Austin and somehow feel like true wilderness ten minutes from downtown.
adventure.bonus: Jump from the Sculpture Falls ledge — at least five feet above the water.

adventure.title: Pedernales Falls State Park
adventure.description: The Pedernales River cascades over tiered limestone shelves in a remote state park that feels nothing like the city you left an hour ago.
adventure.bonus: Cross the river on foot by hopping the limestone slabs without touching the water.

adventure.title: Hamilton Pool Preserve
adventure.description: A collapsed grotto with a 50-foot waterfall spilling into a jade swimming hole forty miles west of the city is one of Texas's most surreal natural landmarks.
adventure.bonus: Wade all the way to the waterfall and stand directly beneath it for ten seconds.

adventure.title: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
adventure.description: Climbing the massive pink granite dome an hour outside Austin rewards you with a panoramic sweep of the Hill Country that genuinely earns the word 'enchanted.'
adventure.bonus: Find the summit crevice cave and squeeze through it.

adventure.title: Barton Springs Pool
adventure.description: A spring-fed natural pool carved into the limestone heart of Zilker Park keeps the water at a brisk 68°F year-round, making every plunge feel like a reset.
adventure.bonus: Swim a full lap across the 900-foot length without stopping.
